episode_title: The Mindset Shifts That Separate the Ultra-Rich from Everyday Investors | Bob Fraser
question: What separates billionaire investors from everyday investors when evaluating investment risk?
transcript_excerpt: Big investors focus first on not losing money. Warren Buffett said the number one rule of investing is don't lose money, and the number two rule is don't forget rule number one. If you have losses, you stop compounding, and a portfolio that is volatile with higher returns actually leaves you with less money at the end of the day than something boring and steady.

episode_title: The Mindset Shifts That Separate the Ultra-Rich from Everyday Investors | Bob Fraser
question: Why is recent market success in individual stocks like NVIDIA not a reliable indicator of future investment performance?
transcript_excerpt: Just because something has gone up does not mean it will continue to go up. Everything goes up until it doesn't, and when everybody who is bullish has already bought, there are no buyers left, only sellers. The price-to-earnings ratio is now in the nosebleed section higher than the dot-com bubble, and based on historical data, we should expect the next 10 years to see about zero or minus 0.1% return for the stock market.

episode_title: The Mindset Shifts That Separate the Ultra-Rich from Everyday Investors | Bob Fraser
question: What are the key characteristics that define alternative investments like private credit?
transcript_excerpt: Alternative investments are professionally managed passive investments where you put money into the deal with no other contribution. Private credit has a superpower of low risk, high cash flows, plus liquidity, offering double-digit returns sometimes with monthly cash flow, fairly safe compared to commercial real estate, and liquidity through four windows per year where investors can access their money.

episode_title: The Mindset Shifts That Separate the Ultra-Rich from Everyday Investors | Bob Fraser
question: How does the SEC regulation Reg D 506C enable alternative investment offerings?
transcript_excerpt: Reg D 506C deals allow you to advertise or market the investment, and if somebody is an accredited investor recognized by the SEC, they are able to invest. Accredited investors are those with a million dollars in assets or net worth outside of their home, or who make $200,000 a year individually or $300,000 as a combined couple, or who have certain certifications.

episode_title: The Mindset Shifts That Separate the Ultra-Rich from Everyday Investors | Bob Fraser
question: What was the origin story behind Aspen Funds' core income fund?
transcript_excerpt: The fund started 14 years ago when a friend with 13 adopted special needs kids came to Bob asking how to earn income from an inheritance. Bob realized he could create an income fund by buying re-performing notes—loans where someone wasn't paying but got a loan modification and started paying again. The fund has never missed a payment, is now $100 million in equity, and that friend was the first investor.

episode_title: The Mindset Shifts That Separate the Ultra-Rich from Everyday Investors | Bob Fraser
question: Why do financial advisors typically discourage their clients from investing in alternative investments?
transcript_excerpt: Financial advisors are very conflicted and do not understand alternatives—it is not a part of their database or knowledge base and is not required to do their tests. They facilitate fear that alts are wing nutty, edgy, fringy, and super risky, though you can make stupid investments in public stocks as well. Bob believes financial advisors serve a valuable need, but very few understand alternatives.

episode_title: The Mindset Shifts That Separate the Ultra-Rich from Everyday Investors | Bob Fraser
question: How does a coding and systems background influence deal underwriting methodology?
transcript_excerpt: A coding background brings very logical and sequential thinking that is systematized, building repeatable systems that measure the same factors over and over. Combined with experience through major market crises, this approach leads to building bulletproof investments with contingency plans, ensuring there is a plan B, plan C, and plan D in case things go wrong.

episode_title: The Mindset Shifts That Separate the Ultra-Rich from Everyday Investors | Bob Fraser
question: What is the most efficient shortcut for due diligence when evaluating investment deals?
transcript_excerpt: The cheapest way to get about 80% of the value out of due diligence is looking at co-investment—how much skin does the sponsor have in their own deal. All deals have promote or carried interest aligning the sponsor with upside, but they are not aligned on the downside, which is the most important thing regarding risk.

episode_title: The Mindset Shifts That Separate the Ultra-Rich from Everyday Investors | Bob Fraser
question: Why do sophisticated investors build diversified portfolios rather than trying to predict market movements?
transcript_excerpt: Billionaire investors do not try to predict the market or where interest rates and geopolitical things are going. Instead, they build a bulletproof portfolio that is resilient in all conditions. When one of five big categories takes a major dip, they rebalance quarterly or yearly, selling the stuff that has gone up and buying the stuff that has gone down, mathematically selling at the top and buying at the bottom.
